stance_summary: Six consecutive holds — but the July vote fractured 9–3 as three regional hawks dissented for an immediate hike. The easing bias is gone, forward guidance abandoned, and the debate has moved entirely to when (not whether) the Fed hikes. September carries roughly 75% hike odds. Warsh: "I asked for a good family fight, and I got one."
policy_outlook: September is now the decision point. The July "hawkish hold" with three dissents leaves the committee one hot inflation print away from its first hike since 2023 — futures price roughly 75% odds of a September move. The wild card is oil: a durable US–Iran pause could pull headline inflation back and unwind the hike trade as fast as it built. Warsh's five task forces report this fall, so a September hike would mean acting before his own reviews conclude.
alert: Hawkish hold, 3 dissents: July 28–29 meeting — FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% but Hammack, Kashkari & Logan dissented for a 25bp hike (first multi-dissent of Warsh's tenure). Warsh: "I asked for a good family fight, and I got one." Markets sold off hard — Dow −1,100 (worst day in over a year), 30Y yield hit highest since 2007. September is now the live meeting: futures price ~75% odds of a hike.

members.name: Kevin Warsh
members.title: Chair, Board of Governors — sworn in May 22
members.note: Held rates at his second meeting (Jul 29) despite three hawkish dissents, choosing to wait rather than prejudge his five task forces due to report this fall. Still refuses forward guidance but noted market tightening is "doing some of the Fed's job." Committed to press conferences through 2026. "I asked for a good family fight, and I got one."

members.name: Jerome Powell
members.title: Board of Governors — permanent voter (former Chair)
members.note: Voted with the majority to hold. Keeping a low profile as promised; no public dissent from the new chair's communication overhaul. His continued Board presence still blocks a White House-preferred appointment.

members.name: Michael Barr
members.title: Vice Chair for Supervision
members.note: Voted for the July hold. Centrist; primarily focused on bank supervision and financial stability. No strong directional lean on rates in recent public statements.

members.name: Michelle Bowman
members.title: Vice Chair for Supervision (acting)
members.note: Voted for the July hold despite prior easing preference. Some participants still see scenarios where inflation eases and allows cuts — Bowman likely among them, but the 4.2% CPI print constrains the dovish case.

members.name: Lisa Cook
members.title: Board of Governors
members.note: Voted for the July hold. Supreme Court removal case still pending. The weak June payrolls print (+57k) supports her employment-focused dovish framework, but 4.2% CPI leaves little room to argue for cuts near-term.
members.latest_source: Jul 29 hold vote; SC case ongoing

members.name: Philip Jefferson
members.title: Vice Chair
members.note: Voted for the July hold. Archetypal centrist and key moderating voice as the committee absorbs Warsh's operational overhaul. Balanced framing, data-dependent.

members.name: Christopher Waller
members.title: Board of Governors
members.note: Voted with the July majority to hold, but has publicly signalled support for tighter policy should inflation persist — a marked shift from his January cut-dissent. Now sits at the hawkish edge of neutral; a possible fourth dissenter if September data runs hot.

members.name: Stephen Miran
members.title: Board of Governors (term expired Jan 31 — serving until successor confirmed)
members.note: Voted with the majority in June and July — no dissents since ending his 2026 streak of cut-dissents at the June meeting. Even the committee's most dovish member has not sustained the easing case against 4.2% CPI.

members.name: John Williams
members.title: NY Fed President — FOMC Vice Chair
members.note: Voted for the July hold. Classic centrist anchor and the institutional bridge between Warsh and the legacy committee.

members.name: Beth Hammack
members.title: Cleveland Fed President
members.note: Dissented again on Jul 29 — this time for an immediate 25bp hike, not just against guidance. Cited the pressure households face from persistently higher prices "across the board." Made the final hawkish case before the pre-meeting blackout. The committee's clearest hawk.

members.name: Neel Kashkari
members.title: Minneapolis Fed President
members.note: Dissented on Jul 29 for a 25bp hike alongside Hammack and Logan. His early-2026 warning that a price shock could unanchor expectations has hardened into an active call for tighter policy now, rather than waiting. Full transition from his historically dovish reputation.

members.name: Lorie Logan
members.title: Dallas Fed President
members.note: Dissented on Jul 29 for a hike, the most specific of the three: she has stated outright that rates should be "modestly" higher. Her line that inflation has been "too high, for too long" is effectively the hawks' slogan.

members.name: Anna Paulson
members.title: Chicago Fed President
members.note: Voted for the July hold. The +57k June payrolls print supports her labor-market concern, and some participants still see scenarios where inflation eases and rates can fall — the dovish tail she represents.
